correctness.rationale: Every multipath in the bidirected two-hub n-leaf graph uses each of four distinct hub/arc colors at most once by indegree/outdegree constraints. Arcs sharing one leaf must form either ordered pair 03 (u→leaf→v) or 12 (v→leaf→u); occupying both would make a directed 4-cycle. Thus leaf-permutation face orbits are exactly color subsets S with partitions into allowed blocks and |blocks|≤n. A setwise simplex stabilizer cannot exchange arcs since each has a unique color, so the geometric quotient (not the naive vertex orbit simplex) is a regular CW complex with distinct color-restriction face incidences. For n≥4 at most four blocks exist; the regular face poset stabilizes with (4,8,8,3) cells. Independently enumerated allowed signatures for n=1..5 and checked all 11 displayed free codimension-one pairs against every surviving higher coface: a single vertex survives at n≥4. At n=3 the stated four additional pairs leave (4,6,4) cells giving a connected closed surface of Euler characteristic 2, hence S²; at n=2 the four two-cells are a tetrahedral sphere with two extra one-cell chords, and n=1 yields two disjoint intervals. This supports S0, S²∨2S¹, S², and contractible types, respectively, including the precise sharp n=4 threshold.
